questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of head or neck injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: By wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always a risk when riding a motorcycle, no matter your speed. Wearing a quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of these injuries.

questions.question: What material offers the best protection in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or synthetic materials
questions.explanation: Leather or synthetic materials provide the best crash protection. Riders should always wear long pants and jackets while riding.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find an alternate route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely and wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing. Never try to drive around a train.

questions.question: What should rider's boots or shoes do?

options.text: Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover their ankles.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: How is alcohol different from other substances?

options.text: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.
It needs to be digested before entering the bloodstream.
It can improve your riding ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It passes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream, quickly reaching the brain.

questions.question: How should jackets and pants fit when riding?

options.text: Loosely so the wind can catch the fabric.
Snugly enough to prevent flapping in the wind.
Tightly so you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly enough to prevent flapping in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind, but loosely enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: What color clothing should you wear when riding during the day?

options.text: Any color because other drivers can see you in daylight.
Dark colors to contrast with sunlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors to increase visibility.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright clothing to be more visible while riding, even during the day.

questions.question: How difficult is it to judge distances when traveling at night?

options.text: It is easier than during the day.
It is about the same as during the day.
It is more difficult than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is more difficult than during the day.
questions.explanation: Judging distances is harder at night than during the day. Shadows and light contrasts help you see how far away objects are. At night, artificial lighting can distort or hide these natural cues.

questions.question: When riding in the left third of a lane to be seen in a car's side mirror, what is the problem?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind can prevent the use of a side mirror.
Motorists should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane where the driver is more likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They inform drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When traveling at night, you should:

options.text: Ride at the same speed as you would during the day.
Ride slower than you would during the day.
Ride faster than you would during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on unfamiliar roads. Slower speed gives you more time to spot and avoid hazards when you cannot see as well.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Keep a safe distance from each other.
Ride as close to each other as possible.
Not worry about the distance between riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from each other.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. This keeps riders close together while maintaining safe following distances.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Wear a jacket only at night.
Wear a jacket only when it is cold.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket.
questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding a motorcycle, even in warm weather.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Keep plenty of space around your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep plenty of space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep plenty of space around your motorcycle to avoid collisions. Maintain this space cushion when following, being followed, passing, being passed, or sharing lanes.

questions.question: To make it easier for other drivers to see you, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing while riding.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing while riding so other drivers can see you more easily. This works during the day and at night.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire has suddenly gone flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of the motorcycle may jerk or sway side to side. Stop riding and check your tires as soon as possible if you feel this movement.

questions.question: If a sign prohibits mopeds on a freeway:

options.text: Mopeds cannot be used on the freeway.
Mopeds can be used only when traffic is moving smoothly.
Mopeds can be used if traveling at 25 mph or slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mopeds cannot be used on the freeway.
questions.explanation: You cannot operate a motor-driven cycle or moped on a freeway or expressway if signs prohibit it. It is illegal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in emergencies.
Should be used together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where should your feet be when riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding. This helps you stay balanced.

questions.question: Which part of the lane is safest?
questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always safest. Change your position based on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: If a rider wears a helmet during a crash, are they more likely to survive?

options.text: Less likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as someone without a helmet.
More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: Allow tailgaters to pass you. Speeding up will not help and may just make them tailgate faster.

questions.question: What happens if you drink one drink before riding?

options.text: Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to ride a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to ride a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can impair your riding skills. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how often should mirrors be checked?

options.text: All riders should check mirrors frequently.
Only the lead rider should check mirrors.
Mirrors should not be checked often because they distract you.

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders should check mirrors frequently.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often when riding in a group. This helps you watch the riders behind you and keep the group together.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit?
questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the rider.
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the rider and hold firmly to the rider's waist or hips. They can hold handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Never sit sidesaddle.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply controlled pressure to both brakes at the same time for the quickest stop. Do not lock the brakes.

questions.question: When stopping with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The motorcycle will slow down, speed up, and turn more slowly. Start slowing earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger traffic gaps.
